name: seo-scout
label: SEO Scout
desc: A weekly scout that bets cheap on emerging keywords — one small content bet shipped as a PR, with dated day-7 verdicts from live Search Console data.
description:
Set up a weekly SEO-scout loop that grows this site's organic clicks by betting on emerging keywords. The strategy: bet cheap on terms that barely exist yet, read a dated day-7 verdict from live data, and double down only on what works — a small site can't outrank incumbents on head terms, but on a term that's two weeks old there is nobody to outrank. Setup is a guided conversation in four steps — confirm each step with me before creating the loop; never create a blind loop.

## Step 1 — The receipt source (Search Console)
- Verify this machine can read LIVE Google Search Console data for the site — an API script, a CLI, or an MCP tool — and run one query as a smoke test. If no read path exists, help me set one up before creating the loop. Every score in this loop comes from live data, never from memory.
- From that first pull, find the breadwinner: the page carrying the largest share of organic clicks. Standing rule: the breadwinner is protected — interlink to it, never experiment on it, and give it a 14-day cooldown from any change.
- Tag the queries that can never click — AI assistants running searches and navigational queries for other people's tools — so they are excluded from every verdict.

## Step 2 — The radar and the map
- Agree my radar for emerging terms: my own bookmarks, feeds, and the niche communities I follow. Keyword tools lag weeks behind what people just started searching — the posts I bookmark today are next month's keywords.
- Build the field map once: pull what competitors rank for plus our own coverage, and sort keywords into three buckets — high-intent hard (attack only from an angle nobody covers), high-intent easy (comparison terms and pages just off page 1 — collect these quick wins), and low-intent easy (where emerging terms live and a new site builds its track record).

## Step 3 — The bet rules (hard rules)
- Each run places AT MOST ONE cheap bet: a one-line thesis ("this will form demand because …"), then one main guide plus up to 4 supporting pages, written in the site's proven winning page shape. Include the "X is dead" / "X vs Y" displacement pages on purpose when a new term kills an old one.
- Do the writing in a fresh git worktree off the main branch and located outside the loop folder — the loop folder is a synced content home, not a workspace — and ship the bet as ONE pull request a human merges. Never place a second bet while the last PR is unmerged.
- Zero qualifying terms this week is a CLEAN SKIP — say so and stop; never lower the bar to hit a count. Skipping several weeks in a row is the system working.
- Never a self-ranking listicle, never date-bumping without content changes, never one-comparison-page-per-competitor at scale — these formats are actively suppressed and can cost the whole site.

## Step 4 — Verdicts, report, dashboard
- Before any new bet, give every open bet a dated day-7 verdict from live data: scale, hold, or leave. Never scale silently, never kill silently — every verdict gets a date and a number.
- Score emerging terms on POSITION and IMPRESSIONS, never clicks — demand hasn't arrived yet, and a clicks goal quits right before the ground ripens. Read the daily series, never averages, and filter zero-impression days (Search Console reports them as position 0, which makes a dead term look like it ranks #1).
- Write one dated markdown report per run with front matter `type: report`, a `title`, and a `date`, and report the site's 28-day organic clicks as a metric. Never copy credentials or API keys into a report or PR.
- Set up the loop's dashboard at creation: a kanban of bets by stage (thesis → live → scaled or left) plus a chart of the clicks metric. Cadence: weekly (Monday morning) is the natural default — confirm it with me. Rankings are rented: when a bet's window closes, move to the next term instead of defending forever.
